{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|隠岐国}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|隠岐国}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|隠岐国}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|隠岐国}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|隠岐国}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|隠岐国}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|隠岐国}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|隠岐国}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|隠岐国}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社}} Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社}} [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]][[Category:11]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社}} [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[Category:qq]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine.== See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社}} [[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category: tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[Category:qq]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine.== See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): - Main hall (1793, Edo period) - Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) - Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also! == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社}} [[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category: tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[Category:qq]] It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback).
