{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province }} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:National Natural Monuments of Japan]] [[Category:refreshing the redirects]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:return the see also]] }} [[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]] [[sn:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] [[en:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine}}

Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|12=draft}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町|12=draft}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|12=draft}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町|12=draft}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|12=draft}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=draft}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|12=draft}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|12=draft}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|12=draft}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|12=draft}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社|12=draft}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:National Natural Monuments of Japan]] [[Category:refreshing the redirects]] [[Category:New]] }} [[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]] [[sn:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] [[en:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine}}

However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|12=draft|12=draft}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|12=draft|12=draft}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft|12=draft}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft|12=draft}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). revision.text:
{{神社 |名称 = 玉若酢命神社 |画像 = [[ファイル: Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG |250px|玉若酢命神社 拝殿]]
拝殿 |所在地 = [[島根県]][[隠岐郡]][[隠岐の島町]]下西701 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=玉若酢命神社|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = 玉若酢命 |社格 = 式内社（小）
[[隠岐国]][[総社]]
旧[[県社]] |創建 = 不詳 |本殿 = 隠岐造茅葺 |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = [[6月5日]] |神事 = 御霊会 （6月5日） }} '''玉若酢命神社'''（たまわかすみことじんじゃ「玉若酢命神社」『日本歴史地名大系 33 島根県の地名』 平凡社、1995年。[https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_tamawakasu.html 玉若酢命神社]（隠岐の島町観光協会）。/たまわかすのみことじんじゃ「玉若酢命神社」『国史大辞典』 吉川弘文館。）は、[[島根県]][[隠岐郡]][[隠岐の島町]]下西にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[県社]]。古くは「若酢大明神」・「総社明神」とも。 == 祭神 == '''玉若酢命'''を[[祭神|主祭神]]とし、[[大己貴命]]・[[須佐之男命]]・[[稲田姫命]]・[[事代主命]]・[[須世理姫命]]を[[配祀]]する。 社伝によると、[[景行天皇]]が[[皇子]]を各国に分置し、[[隠岐国]]に遣わされた大酢別命の御子が玉若酢命であると伝えられている。玉若酢命は、この島の開拓にかかわる[[神 (神道)|神]]と考えられ、当社の[[宮司]]を代々勤める[[社家|神主家]]の[[億岐氏|億岐家]]が古代の[[国造]]を称し、玉若酢命の末裔とされる。ただし景行天皇の皇子に玉若酢命の名は見えず、『[[国造本紀]]』には[[天八現津彦命|観松彦色止命]]の裔・[[十挨彦命]]が[[応神天皇]]の御代に国造へ任命されたと見える。 『日本の神々 -神社と聖地-　7　山陰』谷川健一 編　『日本の神々 -神社と聖地-　7　山陰』　㈱白水社　1985年8月によれば、玉若酢命は『[[記紀]]』には全く登場しない地方神で、その語義は明らかではないのだと言う。しかし、同書では、島内北西部にある[[水若酢神社]]と鎮座地の地理的・歴史的条件が極めて似ていることから、両社祭神に共通する「ワカス」は、この島の開拓に係わる重要な意味を持つ語であったと推測されている。 == 歴史 == 創建の年代は不詳である。[[寛文]]7年（[[1667年]]）の成立と言われる『[[隠州視聴合紀]]　巻之二』の下西村の条には「（当社の）社司を国造と云ふ。渠（かれ）が言に曰く。[[天武天皇]]の勅命ありて之を奉ず。」と記されている。 『[[日本三代実録]]』[[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]13年（[[871年]]）閏[[8月29日]]の条に[[正六位上]]蕤若酢神の[[神階]]を[[従五位下]]へ陞叙すると言う記事があるが、『日本の神々 -神社と聖地-　7　山陰』によれば「蕤」は花が垂れたる様、または冠・旗などに付ける垂れ飾りの意なので、これをタマと訓み、蕤若酢神を当社のこととする意見が強いのだという。上記の『日本三代実録』における記事が当社のことであるなら、これが史料における初見となる。 [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）の『[[延喜式神名帳]]』では周吉郡4座の1つとして小社に列格された。 当社は[[隠岐諸島]][[島後|島後（どうご）]]の旧西郷町の西郊、甲尾山麓の甲野原に鎮座するが、甲野原は「国府の原」の転化であり、当地は古代から[[隠岐国]]の中心地であった。[[国府]]の近くにあった当社は隠岐国[[総社]]とされたが、『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』中世諸国一宮制研究会編　『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』　㈲岩田書院　2000年2月によれば、当社が何時どのような過程を経て隠岐国総社へ転化されたかについては、[[平安時代]]末期の中世的[[国衙]]体制の成立にともなうであろうと推定される以外、史料が欠けていて明らかではないのだと言う。『神道大系　神社編1　総記（上）』神道大系編纂会 編　『神道大系　神社編1　総記（上）』　神道大系編纂会　1986年9月の[[解題]]では、同島に鎮座する[[有木神社]]に合祀されている総神社が隠岐国総社であったが、いつしか当社と混同したとの説を紹介している。 『[[吾妻鏡]]』[[建久]]4年（[[1193年]]）[[12月20日]]の条では、隠岐国[[地頭]]として[[佐々木定綱]]が任じられているが、『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』によれば、以後、国府地域は佐々木氏の直轄領とされ、強力な[[国衙]][[在庁官人|在庁]]による支配が展開されたのだと言う。その後、国府地域は西郷として再編成され、国衙在庁官人の系譜を引くと推定される[[公文]]が西郷地域の支配に当たったのだと述べている。 [[正和]]元年（[[1312年]]）8月の「玉若酢神社棟札写」いずれも億岐家文書。から、この時の造営は西郷公文が聖教泉坊と語らい、[[島前]]を含む多くの人々へ勧請活動を行って実現したものであることがわかるが、『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』では、これが総社が国衙権力機構の行政機関的なあり方から、直接地域社会に基盤を置く独自の宗教施設へ大きく転換する契機となったのではないかと考察されている。 [[貞治]]7年（[[1368年]]）4月15日の「左衛門尉義親奉書写」では、[[藤原義介|藤原朝臣義介]]が「隠岐国惣国造職」に任じられているが、『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』では、「惣国造職」とは惣社国造職のことを指し、総社の宗教的権威向上と再編成を推進するため当社神官を新しく国造と呼ぶこととし、在庁官人と推定される藤原朝臣義介をその任に当てたと考察している。 当社棟札写や『隠岐家古文書抄録』の内容から、[[応安]]7年（[[1374年]]）以後、当社の造営は絶えず[[守護]]もしくは守護代によって行われたことがわかる。この体制は[[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]末期まで続いた。 [[弘治 (日本)|弘治]]3年（[[1557年]]）7月4日の「惣社五月五日祭礼立用注文案」の記述から、東郷・飯田・犬来の3地域の公文が連盟で当社へ納めるべき費用の内容と数量を確認し、[[#神事|御霊会]]がこれら周辺村落の寄進で行われていたことがわかる。これに関し『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』では、当社が守護・[[戦国大名]]権力との関係とは別に、直接その周辺地域の村落に基盤を置く宗教施設としての性格を強めてきたことを意味するもので、そうした新しい情勢への対応の故に、近世社会への移行後も引き続き大きな宗教的勢力を保持し得たと推定している。 『隠州視聴合紀』「巻之四」には隠岐国の神社一覧が記されているが、その前書きに「下西惣社有號隠州神名帳一巻。不知何人所記。随見記之以備博覧。」とあり、当社所蔵の神名帳を写したことがわかる。、『[[国内神名帳|隠岐国神名帳]]』神道大系編纂会 編　『神道大系　神社編1　総記（上）』　神道大系編纂会　1986年9月　に所収されている。[[文化 (元号)|文化]]8年（[[1811年]]）に[[伴信友]]が書写したものを底本とし、その他の諸本を以て校注を加えている。や『[[隠州神名帳]]』『[[群書類従#続群書類従|続群書類従]]　巻第62』に所収されている。[[奥書]]が無いため、成立年代や来歴は不詳である。には「正一位玉若酢大明神」と記され、同じ隠岐の島町の北部の旧五個村郡（こおり）に鎮座する隠岐国[[一宮]]水若酢神社の正三位よりも神階が上であった。 これに関し『日本の神々 -神社と聖地-　7　山陰』では、正一位の神階を[[宗源宣旨]]もしくは隠岐国造の賢しらによるものであろうと考察している。一方、『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』では、当社の神階が水若酢神社より上であったことから見て、水若酢神社が[[中世#日本|中世]]を通じて国鎮守として機能したのかについては疑問の余地があるとし、前述のように当社神主が国造と呼ばれたことから見ても中世隠岐国では実質的に総社が国鎮守である一宮の機能を兼ね、水若酢神社は名目上の一宮に止まった可能性があると述べ、『[[大日本国一宮記]]』が[[由良比女神社]]を隠岐国一宮とした混乱は、こうしたところに原因があったのではないかと推測している。 『隠州視聴合紀　巻之二』の下西村の条では「北の高原に惣社と號して大社あり。[[鳥居|花表]]・[[玉垣|瑞籬]]・拝殿・本宮美しくして、且つ舊りたり。四方の松杉皆大にして、霊場他に異なり。」と[[江戸時代]]初期の当社の様子を伝えている。 [[明治]]の[[近代社格制度]]により、明治5年（[[1872年]]）に県社へ列格された。[[昭和]]10年（[[1935年]]）4月30日には、[[社家]]に伝わる[[駅鈴]]2個と隠伎[[倉印]]1個が国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている。さらに[[平成]]4年（[[1992年]]）1月21日に本殿・随神門・旧拝殿・社家億岐家住宅などが国の[[重要文化財]]に指定された。 == 施設・遺構など == 本殿・随神門・社家億岐家住宅が「玉若酢命神社3棟」として重要文化財に指定され、旧拝殿が附（つけたり）指定となっている。 {| | [[ファイル:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Gate.JPG|250px|鳥居]] | style="width:1em" | | style="vertical-align:top" | '''鳥居'''
[[国道485号]]に面して立つ大鳥居。 |- |} {| style="width:70%" | [[ファイル:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Zuishinmon.JPG|250px|随神門]] | style="width:1em" | | style="vertical-align:top" | '''随神門'''
[[嘉永]]5年（[[1852年]]）の建立。入母屋造茅葺。桁行（正面）柱間は3間だが、八脚門形式ではなく、梁間は1間とする。通路の左右に随神像を安置する。平成4年（1992年）1月21日に国の重要文化財に指定された。文化財建造物の説明は「新指定の文化財」『月刊文化財』341号（第一法規、1992）を参照した。 |- | style="height:1em" | |- | [[ファイル:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Honden.JPG|250px|本殿]] | | style="vertical-align:top" | '''本殿'''
[[本殿]]は[[切妻造]][[茅葺]]、[[妻入]][[妻]]（伝統的木造建築で、屋根立面が三角形に見える側）を正面とし、入口を設けること。。桁行（本建物の場合は側面）2間、梁間（正面）3間の身舎（もや）の正面に檜皮葺きの[[片流れ]]の[[向拝]]を付ける[[隠岐造]]。春日造と異なり、切妻屋根と庇屋根は一体化しておらず構造的に別になっている。[[寛政]]5年（[[1793年]]）の建立で、平成4年（1992年）1月21日に国の重要文化財に指定されている。 |- | style="height:1em" | |- | [[ファイル:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Old Haiden.JPG|250px|旧 拝殿]] | | style="vertical-align:top" | '''旧 拝殿'''
画像一番左の建物が旧拝殿。[[慶応]]2年（[[1866年]]）建立で、平成4年（1992年）1月21日に国の重要文化財「玉若酢命神社3棟」の附（つけたり）として指定された。 |- | style="height:1em" | |- | [[ファイル:Oki's residence.JPEG|250px|社家 億岐家住宅]] | | style="vertical-align:top" | '''社家 億岐家住宅'''
境内に隣接する隠岐地方の代表的な大型民家。入母屋造茅葺きで享和元年（1801年）の建立である。建物は東を正面とし、内部は北側を土間、南側を3室×2列の床上部とする。神棚をまつる「神前の間」（2畳大）や土間下手の「ミソギベヤ」など類例の少ない設備があり社家としての特徴を持っている等の理由から、平成4年（1992年）1月21日に国の重要文化財に指定された。建物とともに宅地も重要文化財に指定されている。現在も社務所・住居として使用されている。 |- |} {| style="width:70%" | [[ファイル:Yaosugi.jpg|250px|八百杉]] | style="width:1em" | | style="vertical-align:top" | '''八百杉'''（やおすぎ）
境内にある[[スギ|杉]]の巨木で、樹齢は1,000年とも2,000年以上ともいわれる。[[若狭国]]からきた[[人魚#八百比丘尼伝説|八百比丘尼]]が参拝の記念に植え、800年後の再訪を約束したことから八百杉と呼ばれるようになったと伝えられる。『隠岐古記集』には、同様の伝承を持つ杉が3本あったが、1本は[[天明|天明年間]]（[[1781年]] - [[1788年]]）に大風で倒れ、もう1本も近年倒れたので現在は1本しか残っていないとの記述がある。また、根元に棲んでいた大蛇が、寝ている間に生きたまま木の中に閉じ込められ、今でも幹に耳をあてると大蛇のいびきが聞こえるとの伝承がある。昭和4年（[[1929年]]）12月17日に国の[[天然記念物]]に指定された。 |- |} === その他 === *神社の北西側の丘陵には、[[玉若酢命神社古墳群]]がある。 == 祭事 == *'''御霊会''' :毎年6月5日に行われる例祭は[[御霊会]]（ごれい）『日本の神々 -神社と聖地-　7　山陰』によれば「ごりょうえ」が訛って「ごれい」と呼ばれるようになったのだと言う。と称され、[[神馬]]入れや[[流鏑馬]]の行事が行われる。祭りの当日、下西、西郷、原田、有木、大久、東郷、飯田、加茂の8地区は、それぞれ禊をさせた馬の鞍に幣を立て、別に[[神輿]]も仕立てて道楽（どうがく）を奏しながら当社へ参集する。『日本の神々 -神社と聖地-　7　山陰』によれば、馬に立てられた幣は[[神籬]]である。参集した馬は公祭式の後、「馬入れ」と称して青竹で叩き勢いを付けた早駆けで曳き入れられる。「馬入れ」の後、今度は当社から神輿を出して少し離れた[[御旅所]]まで神幸を行い、その場所で御田植神事と流鏑馬が行われ祭事は終了する。[[元禄]]13年（[[1700年]]）の記録によれば、かつては島前・島後の全域から48匹の馬が参集したが、あるとき島前からの神船が難破したため祭りが中絶し、その後再興したが参集する馬は島後からの8匹になったのだと言う。また、[[太陽暦]]施行前は5月5日に行う[[端午|端午の節句]]の祭りであったため、現在も[[神饌]]として[[ちまき|粽]]を供える事が守られている。昭和40年（[[1965年]]）5月21日に「玉若酢命神社御霊会風流」として島根県指定の無形民俗文化財となった。 == 文化財 == === 重要文化財（国指定） === [[ファイル:隠岐倉印 (複製).JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|隠伎倉印（複製）}}{{small|[[国立歴史民俗博物館]]展示。}}]] [[ファイル:隠岐国駅鈴 (複製).JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|隠岐国駅鈴（複製）}}{{small|国立歴史民俗博物館展示。}}]] * 玉若酢命神社 3棟（建造物） - 1992年（平成4年）1月21日指定。 ** 本殿（附 棟札6枚、普請文書19冊） - 江戸時代後期、寛政5年（1793年）造営。 ** 随神門（附 棟札1枚、普請文書2冊、旧拝殿1棟、普請文書1冊、境内図1鋪） - 江戸時代末期、嘉永5年（1793年）造営。 ** 社家億岐家住宅（附 福神社1基、家相図1鋪） - 江戸時代後期、享和元年（1801年）造営。 * 銅印 印文「隠伎倉印」（考古資料） - 社家億岐家伝世。1935年（昭和10年）4月30日指定。 * 隠岐国駅鈴（考古資料） - 社家億岐家伝世。1935年（昭和10年）4月30日指定。 === 国の天然記念物 === * 玉若酢命神社の八百スギ - 1929年（昭和4年）12月17日指定。 === 島根県指定文化財 === * 史跡 ** 玉若酢命神社古墳群 - 1972年（昭和47年）7月28日指定。 * 無形民俗文化財 ** 玉若酢命神社御霊会風流 - 1965年（昭和40年）5月21日指定。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} == 参考文献 == *[[塙保己一]] 編　『[[群書類従#続群書類従|続群書類従]]　第3輯　上』　続群書類従完成会　1924年2月　（『隠州神名帳』を所収） *[[黒板勝美]]　國史大系編修会 編　『[[国史大系|國史大系]]　第32巻　[[吾妻鑑]]前編』　[[吉川弘文館|㈱吉川弘文館]]　1964年7月 *黒板勝美　國史大系編修会 編　『國史大系　第4巻　[[日本三代実録]]』　㈱吉川弘文館　1966年4月 *[[谷川健一]] 編集委員代表　『日本庶民生活史料集成　第20巻　探検・紀行・地誌 補遺』　[[三一書房|㈱三一書房]]　1972年7月　（『[[隠州視聴合紀]]』を所収） *谷川健一 編　『日本の神々 -神社と聖地-　7　山陰』　[[白水社|㈱白水社]]　1985年8月 *神道大系編纂会 編　『[[神道大系]]　神社編1　総記（上）』　神道大系編纂会　1986年9月　（『隠岐国神名帳』を所収） *中世諸国一宮制研究会編　『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』　㈲岩田書院　2000年2月 == 関連項目 == *[[隠岐の歴史]] *[[島根県の観光地]] *[[水若酢神社]] *[[有木神社]] == 外部リンク == *{{Commonscat-inline}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:たまわかすみことしんしや}} [[Category:島根県の神社]] [[Category:島根県の旧県社]] [[Category:隠岐国の式内社]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:隠岐国|社0]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:島根県の重要文化財]] [[Category:隠岐の島町の建築物]] [[Category:隠岐の島町の歴史]] [[Category:江戸時代の建築]]

revision.text:
{{神社 |名称 = 玉若酢命神社 |画像 = [[ファイル: Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG |250px|玉若酢命神社 拝殿]]
拝殿 |所在地 = [[島根県]][[隠岐郡]][[隠岐の島町]]下西701 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=玉若酢命神社|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = 玉若酢命 |社格 = 式内社（小）
[[隠岐国]][[総社]]
旧[[県社]] |創建 = 不詳 |本殿 = 隠岐造茅葺 |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = [[6月5日]] |神事 = 御霊会 （6月5日） }} '''玉若酢命神社'''（たまわかすみことじんじゃ「玉若酢命神社」『日本歴史地名大系 33 島根県の地名』 平凡社、1995年。[https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_tamawakasu.html 玉若酢命神社]（隠岐の島町観光協会）。/たまわかすのみことじんじゃ「玉若酢命神社」『国史大辞典』 吉川弘文館。）は、[[島根県]][[隠岐郡]][[隠岐の島町]]下西にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[県社]]。古くは「若酢大明神」・「総社明神」とも。 == 祭神 == '''玉若酢命'''を[[祭神|主祭神]]とし、[[大己貴命]]・[[須佐之男命]]・[[稲田姫命]]・[[事代主命]]・[[須世理姫命]]を[[配祀]]する。 社伝によると、[[景行天皇]]が[[皇子]]を各国に分置し、[[隠岐国]]に遣わされた大酢別命の御子が玉若酢命であると伝えられている。玉若酢命は、この島の開拓にかかわる[[神 (神道)|神]]と考えられ、当社の[[宮司]]を代々勤める[[社家|神主家]]の[[億岐氏|億岐家]]が古代の[[国造]]を称し、玉若酢命の末裔とされる。ただし景行天皇の皇子に玉若酢命の名は見えず、『[[国造本紀]]』には[[天八現津彦命|観松彦色止命]]の裔・[[十挨彦命]]が[[応神天皇]]の御代に国造へ任命されたと見える。 『日本の神々 -神社と聖地-　7　山陰』谷川健一 編　『日本の神々 -神社と聖地-　7　山陰』　㈱白水社　1985年8月によれば、玉若酢命は『[[記紀]]』には全く登場しない地方神で、その語義は明らかではないのだと言う。しかし、同書では、島内北西部にある[[水若酢神社]]と鎮座地の地理的・歴史的条件が極めて似ていることから、両社祭神に共通する「ワカス」は、この島の開拓に係わる重要な意味を持つ語であったと推測されている。 == 歴史 == 創建の年代は不詳である。[[寛文]]7年（[[1667年]]）の成立と言われる『[[隠州視聴合紀]]　巻之二』の下西村の条には「（当社の）社司を国造と云ふ。渠（かれ）が言に曰く。[[天武天皇]]の勅命ありて之を奉ず。」と記されている。 『[[日本三代実録]]』[[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]13年（[[871年]]）閏[[8月29日]]の条に[[正六位上]]蕤若酢神の[[神階]]を[[従五位下]]へ陞叙すると言う記事があるが、『日本の神々 -神社と聖地-　7　山陰』によれば「蕤」は花が垂れたる様、または冠・旗などに付ける垂れ飾りの意なので、これをタマと訓み、蕤若酢神を当社のこととする意見が強いのだという。上記の『日本三代実録』における記事が当社のことであるなら、これが史料における初見となる。 [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）の『[[延喜式神名帳]]』では周吉郡4座の1つとして小社に列格された。 当社は[[隠岐諸島]][[島後|島後（どうご）]]の旧西郷町の西郊、甲尾山麓の甲野原に鎮座するが、甲野原は「国府の原」の転化であり、当地は古代から[[隠岐国]]の中心地であった。[[国府]]の近くにあった当社は隠岐国[[総社]]とされたが、『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』中世諸国一宮制研究会編　『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』　㈲岩田書院　2000年2月によれば、当社が何時どのような過程を経て隠岐国総社へ転化されたかについては、[[平安時代]]末期の中世的[[国衙]]体制の成立にともなうであろうと推定される以外、史料が欠けていて明らかではないのだと言う。『神道大系　神社編1　総記（上）』神道大系編纂会 編　『神道大系　神社編1　総記（上）』　神道大系編纂会　1986年9月の[[解題]]では、同島に鎮座する[[有木神社]]に合祀されている総神社が隠岐国総社であったが、いつしか当社と混同したとの説を紹介している。 『[[吾妻鏡]]』[[建久]]4年（[[1193年]]）[[12月20日]]の条では、隠岐国[[地頭]]として[[佐々木定綱]]が任じられているが、『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』によれば、以後、国府地域は佐々木氏の直轄領とされ、強力な[[国衙]][[在庁官人|在庁]]による支配が展開されたのだと言う。その後、国府地域は西郷として再編成され、国衙在庁官人の系譜を引くと推定される[[公文]]が西郷地域の支配に当たったのだと述べている。 [[正和]]元年（[[1312年]]）8月の「玉若酢神社棟札写」いずれも億岐家文書。から、この時の造営は西郷公文が聖教泉坊と語らい、[[島前]]を含む多くの人々へ勧請活動を行って実現したものであることがわかるが、『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』では、これが総社が国衙権力機構の行政機関的なあり方から、直接地域社会に基盤を置く独自の宗教施設へ大きく転換する契機となったのではないかと考察されている。 [[貞治]]7年（[[1368年]]）4月15日の「左衛門尉義親奉書写」では、[[藤原義介|藤原朝臣義介]]が「隠岐国惣国造職」に任じられているが、『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』では、「惣国造職」とは惣社国造職のことを指し、総社の宗教的権威向上と再編成を推進するため当社神官を新しく国造と呼ぶこととし、在庁官人と推定される藤原朝臣義介をその任に当てたと考察している。 当社棟札写や『隠岐家古文書抄録』の内容から、[[応安]]7年（[[1374年]]）以後、当社の造営は絶えず[[守護]]もしくは守護代によって行われたことがわかる。この体制は[[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]末期まで続いた。 [[弘治 (日本)|弘治]]3年（[[1557年]]）7月4日の「惣社五月五日祭礼立用注文案」の記述から、東郷・飯田・犬来の3地域の公文が連盟で当社へ納めるべき費用の内容と数量を確認し、[[#神事|御霊会]]がこれら周辺村落の寄進で行われていたことがわかる。これに関し『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』では、当社が守護・[[戦国大名]]権力との関係とは別に、直接その周辺地域の村落に基盤を置く宗教施設としての性格を強めてきたことを意味するもので、そうした新しい情勢への対応の故に、近世社会への移行後も引き続き大きな宗教的勢力を保持し得たと推定している。 『隠州視聴合紀』「巻之四」には隠岐国の神社一覧が記されているが、その前書きに「下西惣社有號隠州神名帳一巻。不知何人所記。随見記之以備博覧。」とあり、当社所蔵の神名帳を写したことがわかる。、『[[国内神名帳|隠岐国神名帳]]』神道大系編纂会 編　『神道大系　神社編1　総記（上）』　神道大系編纂会　1986年9月　に所収されている。[[文化 (元号)|文化]]8年（[[1811年]]）に[[伴信友]]が書写したものを底本とし、その他の諸本を以て校注を加えている。や『[[隠州神名帳]]』『[[群書類従#続群書類従|続群書類従]]　巻第62』に所収されている。[[奥書]]が無いため、成立年代や来歴は不詳である。には「正一位玉若酢大明神」と記され、同じ隠岐の島町の北部の旧五個村郡（こおり）に鎮座する隠岐国[[一宮]]水若酢神社の正三位よりも神階が上であった。 これに関し『日本の神々 -神社と聖地-　7　山陰』では、正一位の神階を[[宗源宣旨]]もしくは隠岐国造の賢しらによるものであろうと考察している。一方、『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』では、当社の神階が水若酢神社より上であったことから見て、水若酢神社が[[中世#日本|中世]]を通じて国鎮守として機能したのかについては疑問の余地があるとし、前述のように当社神主が国造と呼ばれたことから見ても中世隠岐国では実質的に総社が国鎮守である一宮の機能を兼ね、水若酢神社は名目上の一宮に止まった可能性があると述べ、『[[大日本国一宮記]]』が[[由良比女神社]]を隠岐国一宮とした混乱は、こうしたところに原因があったのではないかと推測している。 『隠州視聴合紀　巻之二』の下西村の条では「北の高原に惣社と號して大社あり。[[鳥居|花表]]・[[玉垣|瑞籬]]・拝殿・本宮美しくして、且つ舊りたり。四方の松杉皆大にして、霊場他に異なり。」と[[江戸時代]]初期の当社の様子を伝えている。 [[明治]]の[[近代社格制度]]により、明治5年（[[1872年]]）に県社へ列格された。[[昭和]]10年（[[1935年]]）4月30日には、[[社家]]に伝わる[[駅鈴]]2個と隠伎[[倉印]]1個が国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている。さらに[[平成]]4年（[[1992年]]）1月21日に本殿・随神門・旧拝殿・社家億岐家住宅などが国の[[重要文化財]]に指定された。 == 施設・遺構など == 本殿・随神門・社家億岐家住宅が「玉若酢命神社3棟」として重要文化財に指定され、旧拝殿が附（つけたり）指定となっている。 {| | [[ファイル:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Gate.JPG|250px|鳥居]] | style="width:1em" | | style="vertical-align:top" | '''鳥居'''
[[国道485号]]に面して立つ大鳥居。 |- |} {| style="width:70%" | [[ファイル:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Zuishinmon.JPG|250px|随神門]] | style="width:1em" | | style="vertical-align:top" | '''随神門'''
[[嘉永]]5年（[[1852年]]）の建立。入母屋造茅葺。桁行（正面）柱間は3間だが、八脚門形式ではなく、梁間は1間とする。通路の左右に随神像を安置する。平成4年（1992年）1月21日に国の重要文化財に指定された。文化財建造物の説明は「新指定の文化財」『月刊文化財』341号（第一法規、1992）を参照した。 |- | style="height:1em" | |- | [[ファイル:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Honden.JPG|250px|本殿]] | | style="vertical-align:top" | '''本殿'''
[[本殿]]は[[切妻造]][[茅葺]]、[[妻入]][[妻]]（伝統的木造建築で、屋根立面が三角形に見える側）を正面とし、入口を設けること。。桁行（本建物の場合は側面）2間、梁間（正面）3間の身舎（もや）の正面に檜皮葺きの[[片流れ]]の[[向拝]]を付ける[[隠岐造]]。春日造と異なり、切妻屋根と庇屋根は一体化しておらず構造的に別になっている。[[寛政]]5年（[[1793年]]）の建立で、平成4年（1992年）1月21日に国の重要文化財に指定されている。 |- | style="height:1em" | |- | [[ファイル:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Old Haiden.JPG|250px|旧 拝殿]] | | style="vertical-align:top" | '''旧 拝殿'''
画像一番左の建物が旧拝殿。[[慶応]]2年（[[1866年]]）建立で、平成4年（1992年）1月21日に国の重要文化財「玉若酢命神社3棟」の附（つけたり）として指定された。 |- | style="height:1em" | |- | [[ファイル:Oki's residence.JPEG|250px|社家 億岐家住宅]] | | style="vertical-align:top" | '''社家 億岐家住宅'''
境内に隣接する隠岐地方の代表的な大型民家。入母屋造茅葺きで享和元年（1801年）の建立である。建物は東を正面とし、内部は北側を土間、南側を3室×2列の床上部とする。神棚をまつる「神前の間」（2畳大）や土間下手の「ミソギベヤ」など類例の少ない設備があり社家としての特徴を持っている等の理由から、平成4年（1992年）1月21日に国の重要文化財に指定された。建物とともに宅地も重要文化財に指定されている。現在も社務所・住居として使用されている。 |- |} {| style="width:70%" | [[ファイル:Yaosugi.jpg|250px|八百杉]] | style="width:1em" | | style="vertical-align:top" | '''八百杉'''（やおすぎ）
境内にある[[スギ|杉]]の巨木で、樹齢は1,000年とも2,000年以上ともいわれる。[[若狭国]]からきた[[人魚#八百比丘尼伝説|八百比丘尼]]が参拝の記念に植え、800年後の再訪を約束したことから八百杉と呼ばれるようになったと伝えられる。『隠岐古記集』には、同様の伝承を持つ杉が3本あったが、1本は[[天明|天明年間]]（[[1781年]] - [[1788年]]）に大風で倒れ、もう1本も近年倒れたので現在は1本しか残っていないとの記述がある。また、根元に棲んでいた大蛇が、寝ている間に生きたまま木の中に閉じ込められ、今でも幹に耳をあてると大蛇のいびきが聞こえるとの伝承がある。昭和4年（[[1929年]]）12月17日に国の[[天然記念物]]に指定された。 |- |} === その他 === *神社の北西側の丘陵には、[[玉若酢命神社古墳群]]がある。 == 祭事 == *'''御霊会''' :毎年6月5日に行われる例祭は[[御霊会]]（ごれい）『日本の神々 -神社と聖地-　7　山陰』によれば「ごりょうえ」が訛って「ごれい」と呼ばれるようになったのだと言う。と称され、[[神馬]]入れや[[流鏑馬]]の行事が行われる。祭りの当日、下西、西郷、原田、有木、大久、東郷、飯田、加茂の8地区は、それぞれ禊をさせた馬の鞍に幣を立て、別に[[神輿]]も仕立てて道楽（どうがく）を奏しながら当社へ参集する。『日本の神々 -神社と聖地-　7　山陰』によれば、馬に立てられた幣は[[神籬]]である。参集した馬は公祭式の後、「馬入れ」と称して青竹で叩き勢いを付けた早駆けで曳き入れられる。「馬入れ」の後、今度は当社から神輿を出して少し離れた[[御旅所]]まで神幸を行い、その場所で御田植神事と流鏑馬が行われ祭事は終了する。[[元禄]]13年（[[1700年]]）の記録によれば、かつては島前・島後の全域から48匹の馬が参集したが、あるとき島前からの神船が難破したため祭りが中絶し、その後再興したが参集する馬は島後からの8匹になったのだと言う。また、[[太陽暦]]施行前は5月5日に行う[[端午|端午の節句]]の祭りであったため、現在も[[神饌]]として[[ちまき|粽]]を供える事が守られている。昭和40年（[[1965年]]）5月21日に「玉若酢命神社御霊会風流」として島根県指定の無形民俗文化財となった。 == 文化財 == === 重要文化財（国指定） === [[ファイル:隠岐倉印 (複製).JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|隠伎倉印（複製）}}{{small|[[国立歴史民俗博物館]]展示。}}]] [[ファイル:隠岐国駅鈴 (複製).JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|隠岐国駅鈴（複製）}}{{small|国立歴史民俗博物館展示。}}]] * 玉若酢命神社 3棟（建造物） - 1992年（平成4年）1月21日指定。 ** 本殿（附 棟札6枚、普請文書19冊） - 江戸時代後期、寛政5年（1793年）造営。 ** 随神門（附 棟札1枚、普請文書2冊、旧拝殿1棟、普請文書1冊、境内図1鋪） - 江戸時代末期、嘉永5年（1793年）造営。 ** 社家億岐家住宅（附 福神社1基、家相図1鋪） - 江戸時代後期、享和元年（1801年）造営。 * 銅印 印文「隠伎倉印」（考古資料） - 社家億岐家伝世。1935年（昭和10年）4月30日指定。 * 隠岐国駅鈴（考古資料） - 社家億岐家伝世。1935年（昭和10年）4月30日指定。 === 国の天然記念物 === * 玉若酢命神社の八百スギ - 1929年（昭和4年）12月17日指定。 === 島根県指定文化財 === * 史跡 ** 玉若酢命神社古墳群 - 1972年（昭和47年）7月28日指定。 * 無形民俗文化財 ** 玉若酢命神社御霊会風流 - 1965年（昭和40年）5月21日指定。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} == 参考文献 == *[[塙保己一]] 編　『[[群書類従#続群書類従|続群書類従]]　第3輯　上』　続群書類従完成会　1924年2月　（『隠州神名帳』を所収） *[[黒板勝美]]　國史大系編修会 編　『[[国史大系|國史大系]]　第32巻　[[吾妻鑑]]前編』　[[吉川弘文館|㈱吉川弘文館]]　1964年7月 *黒板勝美　國史大系編修会 編　『國史大系　第4巻　[[日本三代実録]]』　㈱吉川弘文館　1966年4月 *[[谷川健一]] 編集委員代表　『日本庶民生活史料集成　第20巻　探検・紀行・地誌 補遺』　[[三一書房|㈱三一書房]]　1972年7月　（『[[隠州視聴合紀]]』を所収） *谷川健一 編　『日本の神々 -神社と聖地-　7　山陰』　[[白水社|㈱白水社]]　1985年8月 *神道大系編纂会 編　『[[神道大系]]　神社編1　総記（上）』　神道大系編纂会　1986年9月　（『隠岐国神名帳』を所収） *中世諸国一宮制研究会編　『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』　㈲岩田書院　2000年2月 == 関連項目 == *[[隠岐の歴史]] *[[島根県の観光地]] *[[水若酢神社]] *[[有木神社]] == 外部リンク == *{{Commonscat-inline}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:たまわかすみことしんしや}} [[Category:島根県の神社]] [[Category:島根県の旧県社]] [[Category:隠岐国の式内社]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:隠岐国|社0]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:島根県の重要文化財]] [[Category:隠岐の島町の建築物]] [[Category:隠岐の島町の歴史]] [[Category:江戸時代の建築]]

{{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine (玉若酢命神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|250px|Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Haiden]]
Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:National Natural Monuments of Japan]] [[Category:New]] }} [[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]] [[sn:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] [[en:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine}} {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}}

Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|ja|隠岐郡|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_Rank = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|ja|隠岐の島町|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|1=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|ja|水若酢神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine}} {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:National Natural Monuments of Japan]] [[Category:New]] }} [[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]] [[sn:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] [[en:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]]

It is a designated {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|1=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Haiden |location = [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], [[:en:Oki District, Shimane|Oki District, Shimane]], [[:en:Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima, Shimane]], Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[:en:Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima, Shimane]], Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}, and under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushinadahime|qq=}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|qq=}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|qq=}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inshū Shichō Gōki|qq=}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]] in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''[[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]]''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Province|qq=}} * [[:en:Mizuwakasu Shrine|Mizuwakasu Shrine]] {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:National Natural Monuments of Japan]] }} [[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]] [[sn:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] [[en:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]]

Haiden |location = [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], [[:en:Oki District, Shimane|Oki District, Shimane]], [[:en:Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima, Shimane]], Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[:en:Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima, Shimane]], Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}, and under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushinadahime|qq=}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|qq=}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|qq=}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inshū Shichō Gōki|qq=}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]] in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''[[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]]''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Province|qq=}} * [[:en:Mizuwakasu Shrine|Mizuwakasu Shrine]] {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:National Natural Monuments of Japan]] }} [[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]] [[sn:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] [[en:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:島根県の重要文化財]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:隠岐の島町の建築物]] [[Category:隠岐の島町の歴史]] [[Category:隠岐国]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Oki Province]]

Haiden |location = [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], [[:en:Oki District, Shimane|Oki District, Shimane]], [[:en:Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima, Shimane]], Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[:en:Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima, Shimane]], Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushinadahime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to クシナダヒメ}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノヒボコ}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inshū Shichō Gōki|qq=}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]] in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''[[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]]''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Province|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * [[:en:Mizuwakasu Shrine|Mizuwakasu Shrine]] {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] }} [[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]] [[sn:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Shimane prefecture]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[Category:Architecture of Okinoshima Town]] [[Category:Municipal History of Okinoshima]] [[Category:Oki Province]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Oki Province]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[sn:Shikinaisha]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[sn:Shikinaisha]] {{Commons category|Tamawakasumikoto-jinja}} [[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]]

Haiden |location = [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], [[:en:Oki District, Shimane|Oki District, Shimane]], [[:en:Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima, Shimane]], Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[:en:Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima, Shimane]], Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushinadahime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to クシナダヒメ}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノヒボコ}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inshū Shichō Gōki|qq=}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]] in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''[[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]]''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Province|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * [[:en:Mizuwakasu Shrine|Mizuwakasu Shrine]] {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] }} [[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]] [[sn:Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine]] [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Shimane prefecture]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[Category:Architecture of Okinoshima Town]] [[Category:Municipal History of Okinoshima]] [[Category:Oki Province]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Oki Province]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[sn:Shikinaisha]][[sn:Tamawakasu-no-mikoto Shrine]][[sn:Shikinaisha]] {{Commons category|Tamawakasumikoto-jinja}} [[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]]

It is a designated {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushinadahime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to クシナダヒメ}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノヒボコ}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inshū Shichō Gōki|qq=}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]] in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''[[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]]''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki (June 5)|qq=draft|qq=draft|location = {{ill|Okinoshima|qid=Q1205039}} |architecture_style = {{ill|Oki-zukuri|qid=Q11659055}} }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|玉若酢命神社}}, ''Tamawakasu Mikoto Jinja'') is a Shinto shrine located in Shimonishi, Okinoshima Town, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} and served as the [[:en:Sōja|Sōja]] of [[:en:Oki Province|Oki Province]]. The shrine holds historical importance and is designated as a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates '''Tamawakasu Mikoto''' as the principal deity. Additional deities include: * '''Ōnamuchi no Mikoto''' (Ōkuninushi) * '''Susanoo no Mikoto''' * '''Inadahime no Mikoto''' * '''Kotoshironushi no Mikoto''' * '''Suserihime no Mikoto''' According to legend, Tamawakasu Mikoto was the child of Ōsubetsu no Mikoto, dispatched to develop the Oki Islands. The shrine's priestly lineage, the Oki family, claims descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. == Historical Background == The shrine's founding date is uncertain. It is mentioned in historical records such as the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (871), where the deity "Ruiwakasu no Kami" was elevated to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The shrine later became the Sōja of Oki Province, located near the provincial capital. In 1872, under the modern shrine Ranking system, the shrine was designated a prefectural shrine. It houses valuable historical artifacts, including imperial seals and ritual tools. == Architectural Features == The shrine complex includes: * '''main hall (Honden)''': Constructed in 1793 in the Oki-zukuri style, featuring a thatched roof and separated eaves for the main building and porch. * '''Zuishinmon Gate''': Built in 1852, it serves as the entrance to the sacred grounds. * '''Former Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Designated as an auxiliary Important Cultural Property. * '''Oki Family Residence''': A historic house serving as the priest's residence, reflecting the architectural style of 1801. == Cultural Significance == The shrine is closely tied to local history and culture. It houses: * '''Goryōe festival''': An annual event held on June 5, featuring rituals such as horse racing and portable shrine processions. * '''Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar)''': A sacred tree over 1,000 years old, associated with local myths, including the legend of Yao Bikuni. * '''Oki Province Relics''': Imperial seals and bells used historically in administrative functions. == Designations == The shrine and its associated artifacts hold the following designations: * '''Important Cultural Property''' (1992): Includes the main hall, gate, and Oki family residence. * '''National Natural Monument''': Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar) * '''Prefectural Cultural Property''': Includes the Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Kofuns and the Goryōe festival. == Access and location == The shrine is located near historical provincial government ruins and remains a cultural hub for Okinoshima Town. Visitors can view its traditional architecture and partake in its vibrant festivals. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[:en:Oki Islands|Oki Islands]] * [[:en:Sōja|Sōja]] * [[Japanese mythology]] == External Links == * [https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_tamawakasu.html Oki Tourism - Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine] (Japanese) * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Oki Shrines}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Okinoshima, Shimane]] [[Category:Japanese mythology]] }} [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] [[Category:Added translation template]]{{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[Category:Former_Prefectural_Shrines_in_Shimane_Prefecture]] [[Category:島根県の Important Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Edo_period_architecture]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments (buildings)]] [[Category:Architecture of Okinoshima Town]] [[Category:Municipal History of Okinoshima]] [[Category:Oki Province]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Oki Province]] {{wikidata link|Q11572773}}

Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushinadahime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to クシナダヒメ}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノヒボコ}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inshū Shichō Gōki|qq=}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]] in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''[[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]]''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki (June 5)|qq=draft|qq=draft|location = {{ill|Okinoshima|qid=Q1205039}} |architecture_style = {{ill|Oki-zukuri|qid=Q11659055}} }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|玉若酢命神社}}, ''Tamawakasu Mikoto Jinja'') is a Shinto shrine located in Shimonishi, Okinoshima Town, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} and served as the [[:en:Sōja|Sōja]] of [[:en:Oki Province|Oki Province]]. The shrine holds historical importance and is designated as a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates '''Tamawakasu Mikoto''' as the principal deity. Additional deities include: * '''Ōnamuchi no Mikoto''' (Ōkuninushi) * '''Susanoo no Mikoto''' * '''Inadahime no Mikoto''' * '''Kotoshironushi no Mikoto''' * '''Suserihime no Mikoto''' According to legend, Tamawakasu Mikoto was the child of Ōsubetsu no Mikoto, dispatched to develop the Oki Islands. The shrine's priestly lineage, the Oki family, claims descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. == Historical Background == The shrine's founding date is uncertain. It is mentioned in historical records such as the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (871), where the deity "Ruiwakasu no Kami" was elevated to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The shrine later became the Sōja of Oki Province, located near the provincial capital. In 1872, under the modern shrine Ranking system, the shrine was designated a prefectural shrine. It houses valuable historical artifacts, including imperial seals and ritual tools. == Architectural Features == The shrine complex includes: * '''main hall (Honden)''': Constructed in 1793 in the Oki-zukuri style, featuring a thatched roof and separated eaves for the main building and porch. * '''Zuishinmon Gate''': Built in 1852, it serves as the entrance to the sacred grounds. * '''Former Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Designated as an auxiliary Important Cultural Property. * '''Oki Family Residence''': A historic house serving as the priest's residence, reflecting the architectural style of 1801. == Cultural Significance == The shrine is closely tied to local history and culture. It houses: * '''Goryōe festival''': An annual event held on June 5, featuring rituals such as horse racing and portable shrine processions. * '''Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar)''': A sacred tree over 1,000 years old, associated with local myths, including the legend of Yao Bikuni. * '''Oki Province Relics''': Imperial seals and bells used historically in administrative functions. == Designations == The shrine and its associated artifacts hold the following designations: * '''Important Cultural Property''' (1992): Includes the main hall, gate, and Oki family residence. * '''National Natural Monument''': Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar) * '''Prefectural Cultural Property''': Includes the Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Kofuns and the Goryōe festival. == Access and location == The shrine is located near historical provincial government ruins and remains a cultural hub for Okinoshima Town. Visitors can view its traditional architecture and partake in its vibrant festivals. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[:en:Oki Islands|Oki Islands]] * [[:en:Sōja|Sōja]] * [[Japanese mythology]] == External Links == * [https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_tamawakasu.html Oki Tourism - Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine] (Japanese) * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Oki Shrines}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Okinoshima, Shimane]] [[Category:Japanese mythology]] }} [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] [[Category:Added translation template]]{{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[Category:Former_Prefectural_Shrines_in_Shimane_Prefecture]] [[Category:島根県の Important Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Edo_period_architecture]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments (buildings)]] [[Category:Architecture of Okinoshima Town]] [[Category:Municipal History of Okinoshima]] [[Category:Oki Province]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Oki Province]] {{wikidata link|Q11572773}}
