Haiden |location = [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], [[:en:Oki District, Shimane|Oki District, Shimane]], [[:en:Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima, Shimane]], Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[:en:Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima, Shimane]], Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushinadahime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to クシナダヒメ}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノヒボコ}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inshū Shichō Gōki|qq=}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]] in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''[[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]]''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * [[:en:Mizuwakasu Shrine|Mizuwakasu Shrine]] {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{Commons category|Tamawakasumikoto-jinja}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11572773]] Wikidata name: Tamawakasu-mikoto Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:49, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine |image = File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG |location = Shimane Prefecture, Oki District, Okinoshima Town, Shimonishi 701, Japan |coordinates = {{Coord|36.207083|N|133.312556|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (Minor Shrine), [[:en:Sōja|Sōja]] of [[:en:Oki Province|Oki Province]], Former Prefectural Shrine|establishment = Unknown |architecture = Oki-zukuri (Thatch Roof Style) |annual_festival = [[June 5]] |rituals = Goryōe (June 5)|location = {{ill|Okinoshima|WD=Q1205039}} |architecture_style = {{ill|Oki-zukuri|WD=Q11659055}} }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|玉若酢命神社}}, ''Tamawakasu Mikoto Jinja'') is a Shinto shrine located in Shimonishi, Okinoshima Town, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} and served as the [[:en:Sōja|Sōja]] of [[:en:Oki Province|Oki Province]]. The shrine holds historical importance and is designated as a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates '''Tamawakasu Mikoto''' as the principal deity. Additional deities include: * '''Ōnamuchi no Mikoto''' (Ōkuninushi) * '''Susanoo no Mikoto''' * '''Inadahime no Mikoto''' * '''Kotoshironushi no Mikoto''' * '''Suserihime no Mikoto''' According to legend, Tamawakasu Mikoto was the child of Ōsubetsu no Mikoto, dispatched to develop the Oki Islands. The shrine's priestly lineage, the Oki family, claims descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. == Historical Background == The shrine's founding date is uncertain. It is mentioned in historical records such as the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (871), where the deity "Ruiwakasu no Kami" was elevated to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The shrine later became the Sōja of Oki Province, located near the provincial capital. In 1872, under the modern shrine Ranking system, the shrine was designated a prefectural shrine. It houses valuable historical artifacts, including imperial seals and ritual tools. == Architectural Features == The shrine complex includes: * '''main hall (Honden)''': Constructed in 1793 in the Oki-zukuri style, featuring a thatched roof and separated eaves for the main building and porch. * '''Zuishinmon Gate''': Built in 1852, it serves as the entrance to the sacred grounds. * '''Former Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Designated as an auxiliary Important Cultural Property. * '''Oki Family Residence''': A historic house serving as the priest's residence, reflecting the architectural style of 1801. == Cultural Significance == The shrine is closely tied to local history and culture. It houses: * '''Goryōe festival''': An annual event held on June 5, featuring rituals such as horse racing and portable shrine processions. * '''Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar)''': A sacred tree over 1,000 years old, associated with local myths, including the legend of Yao Bikuni. * '''Oki Province Relics''': Imperial seals and bells used historically in administrative functions. == Designations == The shrine and its associated artifacts hold the following designations: * '''Important Cultural Property''' (1992): Includes the main hall, gate, and Oki family residence. * '''National Natural Monument''': Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar) * '''Prefectural Cultural Property''': Includes the Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Kofuns and the Goryōe festival. == Access and location == The shrine is located near historical provincial government ruins and remains a cultural hub for Okinoshima Town. Visitors can view its traditional architecture and partake in its vibrant festivals. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[:en:Oki Islands|Oki Islands]] * [[:en:Sōja|Sōja]] * [[Japanese mythology]] == External Links == * [https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_tamawakasu.html Oki Tourism - Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine] (Japanese) * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Oki Shrines}} {{Sōja shrines}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{wikidata link|Q11572773}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Added translation template]] [[Category:Architecture of Okinoshima Town]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Edo_period_architecture]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Former_Prefectural_Shrines_in_Shimane_Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Shimane prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese mythology]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Municipal History of Okinoshima]] [[Category:Oki Province]] [[Category:Okinoshima, Shimane]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Oki Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Special:LonelyPages November 4 2025]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:島根県の Important Cultural Properties]]

Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|en|Shimane Prefecture|WD=Q132751|lt=Shimane Prefecture}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|en|Oki District, Shimane|WD=Q735735|lt=Oki District, Shimane}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|en|Okinoshima, Shimane|WD=Q1205039|lt=Okinoshima, Shimane}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|en|Okinoshima, Shimane|WD=Q1205039|lt=Okinoshima, Shimane}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|WD=Q712534|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushinadahime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to クシナダヒメ}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノヒボコ}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inshū Shichō Gōki|qq=}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|WD=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|en|Mizuwakasu Shrine|WD=Q11549109|lt=Mizuwakasu Shrine}} {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{Commons category|Tamawakasumikoto-jinja}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11572773]] Wikidata name: Tamawakasu-mikoto Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:49, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine |image = File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG |location = Shimane Prefecture, Oki District, Okinoshima Town, Shimonishi 701, Japan |coordinates = {{Coord|36.207083|N|133.312556|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (Minor Shrine), {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} of {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|WD=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province}}, Former Prefectural Shrine|establishment = Unknown |architecture = Oki-zukuri (Thatch Roof Style) |annual_festival = [[June 5]] |rituals = Goryōe (June 5)|location = {{ill|Okinoshima|WD=Q1205039}} |architecture_style = {{ill|Oki-zukuri|WD=Q11659055}} }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|玉若酢命神社}}, ''Tamawakasu Mikoto Jinja'') is a Shinto shrine located in Shimonishi, Okinoshima Town, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} and served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} of {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|WD=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province}}. The shrine holds historical importance and is designated as a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates '''Tamawakasu Mikoto''' as the principal deity. Additional deities include: * '''Ōnamuchi no Mikoto''' (Ōkuninushi) * '''Susanoo no Mikoto''' * '''Inadahime no Mikoto''' * '''Kotoshironushi no Mikoto''' * '''Suserihime no Mikoto''' According to legend, Tamawakasu Mikoto was the child of Ōsubetsu no Mikoto, dispatched to develop the Oki Islands. The shrine's priestly lineage, the Oki family, claims descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. == Historical Background == The shrine's founding date is uncertain. It is mentioned in historical records such as the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (871), where the deity "Ruiwakasu no Kami" was elevated to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The shrine later became the Sōja of Oki Province, located near the provincial capital. In 1872, under the modern shrine Ranking system, the shrine was designated a prefectural shrine. It houses valuable historical artifacts, including imperial seals and ritual tools. == Architectural Features == The shrine complex includes: * '''main hall (Honden)''': Constructed in 1793 in the Oki-zukuri style, featuring a thatched roof and separated eaves for the main building and porch. * '''Zuishinmon Gate''': Built in 1852, it serves as the entrance to the sacred grounds. * '''Former Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Designated as an auxiliary Important Cultural Property. * '''Oki Family Residence''': A historic house serving as the priest's residence, reflecting the architectural style of 1801. == Cultural Significance == The shrine is closely tied to local history and culture. It houses: * '''Goryōe festival''': An annual event held on June 5, featuring rituals such as horse racing and portable shrine processions. * '''Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar)''': A sacred tree over 1,000 years old, associated with local myths, including the legend of Yao Bikuni. * '''Oki Province Relics''': Imperial seals and bells used historically in administrative functions. == Designations == The shrine and its associated artifacts hold the following designations: * '''Important Cultural Property''' (1992): Includes the main hall, gate, and Oki family residence. * '''National Natural Monument''': Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar) * '''Prefectural Cultural Property''': Includes the Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Kofuns and the Goryōe festival. == Access and location == The shrine is located near historical provincial government ruins and remains a cultural hub for Okinoshima Town. Visitors can view its traditional architecture and partake in its vibrant festivals. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Islands|en|Oki Islands|WD=Q483146|lt=Oki Islands}} * {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} * [[Japanese mythology]] == External Links == * [https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_tamawakasu.html Oki Tourism - Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine] (Japanese) * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Oki Shrines}} {{Sōja shrines}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{wikidata link|Q11572773}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Added translation template]] [[Category:Architecture of Okinoshima Town]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Edo_period_architecture]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Former_Prefectural_Shrines_in_Shimane_Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Shimane prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese mythology]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Municipal History of Okinoshima]] [[Category:Oki Province]] [[Category:Okinoshima, Shimane]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Oki Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Special:LonelyPages November 4 2025]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:島根県の Important Cultural Properties]]

Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|en|Shimane Prefecture|WD=Q132751|lt=Shimane Prefecture}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|en|Oki District, Shimane|WD=Q735735|lt=Oki District, Shimane}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|en|Okinoshima, Shimane|WD=Q1205039|lt=Okinoshima, Shimane}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|en|Okinoshima, Shimane|WD=Q1205039|lt=Okinoshima, Shimane}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|WD=Q712534|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushinadahime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to クシナダヒメ}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノヒボコ}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inshū Shichō Gōki|qq=}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|WD=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|en|Mizuwakasu Shrine|WD=Q11549109|lt=Mizuwakasu Shrine}} {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{Commons category|Tamawakasumikoto-jinja}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11572773]] Wikidata name: Tamawakasu-mikoto Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:49, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine |image = File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG |location = Shimane Prefecture, Oki District, Okinoshima Town, Shimonishi 701, Japan |coordinates = {{Coord|36.207083|N|133.312556|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (Minor Shrine), {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} of {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|WD=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province}}, Former Prefectural Shrine|establishment = Unknown |architecture = Oki-zukuri (Thatch Roof Style) |annual_festival = [[June 5]] |rituals = Goryōe (June 5)|location = {{ill|Okinoshima|WD=Q1205039}} |architecture_style = {{ill|Oki-zukuri|WD=Q11659055}} }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|玉若酢命神社}}, ''Tamawakasu Mikoto Jinja'') is a Shinto shrine located in Shimonishi, Okinoshima Town, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} and served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} of {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|WD=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province}}. The shrine holds historical importance and is designated as a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates '''Tamawakasu Mikoto''' as the principal deity. Additional deities include: * '''Ōnamuchi no Mikoto''' (Ōkuninushi) * '''Susanoo no Mikoto''' * '''Inadahime no Mikoto''' * '''Kotoshironushi no Mikoto''' * '''Suserihime no Mikoto''' According to legend, Tamawakasu Mikoto was the child of Ōsubetsu no Mikoto, dispatched to develop the Oki Islands. The shrine's priestly lineage, the Oki family, claims descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. == Historical Background == The shrine's founding date is uncertain. It is mentioned in historical records such as the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (871), where the deity "Ruiwakasu no Kami" was elevated to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The shrine later became the Sōja of Oki Province, located near the provincial capital. In 1872, under the modern shrine Ranking system, the shrine was designated a prefectural shrine. It houses valuable historical artifacts, including imperial seals and ritual tools. == Architectural Features == The shrine complex includes: * '''main hall (Honden)''': Constructed in 1793 in the Oki-zukuri style, featuring a thatched roof and separated eaves for the main building and porch. * '''Zuishinmon Gate''': Built in 1852, it serves as the entrance to the sacred grounds. * '''Former Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Designated as an auxiliary Important Cultural Property. * '''Oki Family Residence''': A historic house serving as the priest's residence, reflecting the architectural style of 1801. == Cultural Significance == The shrine is closely tied to local history and culture. It houses: * '''Goryōe festival''': An annual event held on June 5, featuring rituals such as horse racing and portable shrine processions. * '''Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar)''': A sacred tree over 1,000 years old, associated with local myths, including the legend of Yao Bikuni. * '''Oki Province Relics''': Imperial seals and bells used historically in administrative functions. == Designations == The shrine and its associated artifacts hold the following designations: * '''Important Cultural Property''' (1992): Includes the main hall, gate, and Oki family residence. * '''National Natural Monument''': Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar) * '''Prefectural Cultural Property''': Includes the Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Kofuns and the Goryōe festival. == Access and location == The shrine is located near historical provincial government ruins and remains a cultural hub for Okinoshima Town. Visitors can view its traditional architecture and partake in its vibrant festivals. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Islands|en|Oki Islands|WD=Q483146|lt=Oki Islands}} * {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} * [[Japanese mythology]] == External Links == * [https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_tamawakasu.html Oki Tourism - Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine] (Japanese) * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Oki Shrines}} {{Sōja shrines}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{wikidata link|Q11572773}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Added translation template]] [[Category:Architecture of Okinoshima Town]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Edo_period_architecture]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Former_Prefectural_Shrines_in_Shimane_Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Shimane prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese mythology]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Municipal History of Okinoshima]] [[Category:Oki Province]] [[Category:Okinoshima, Shimane]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Oki Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Special:LonelyPages November 4 2025]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:島根県の Important Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Junior Fifth Rank]] [[Category:Senior Sixth Rank]] [[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]]

Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|en|Shimane Prefecture|WD=Q132751|lt=Shimane Prefecture}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|en|Oki District, Shimane|WD=Q735735|lt=Oki District, Shimane}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|en|Okinoshima, Shimane|WD=Q1205039|lt=Okinoshima, Shimane}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|en|Okinoshima, Shimane|WD=Q1205039|lt=Okinoshima, Shimane}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|WD=Q712534|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushinadahime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to クシナダヒメ}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノヒボコ}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inshū Shichō Gōki|qq=}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|WD=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|en|Mizuwakasu Shrine|WD=Q11549109|lt=Mizuwakasu Shrine}} {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{Commons category|Tamawakasumikoto-jinja}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11572773]] Wikidata name: Tamawakasu-mikoto Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:49, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine |image = File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG |location = Shimane Prefecture, Oki District, Okinoshima Town, Shimonishi 701, Japan |coordinates = {{Coord|36.207083|N|133.312556|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (Minor Shrine), {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} of {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|WD=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province}}, Former Prefectural Shrine|establishment = Unknown |architecture = Oki-zukuri (Thatch Roof Style) |annual_festival = [[June 5]] |rituals = Goryōe (June 5)|location = {{ill|Okinoshima|WD=Q1205039}} |architecture_style = {{ill|Oki-zukuri|WD=Q11659055}} }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|玉若酢命神社}}, ''Tamawakasu Mikoto Jinja'') is a Shinto shrine located in Shimonishi, Okinoshima Town, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} and served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} of {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|WD=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province}}. The shrine holds historical importance and is designated as a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates '''Tamawakasu Mikoto''' as the principal deity. Additional deities include: * '''Ōnamuchi no Mikoto''' (Ōkuninushi) * '''Susanoo no Mikoto''' * '''Inadahime no Mikoto''' * '''Kotoshironushi no Mikoto''' * '''Suserihime no Mikoto''' According to legend, Tamawakasu Mikoto was the child of Ōsubetsu no Mikoto, dispatched to develop the Oki Islands. The shrine's priestly lineage, the Oki family, claims descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. == Historical Background == The shrine's founding date is uncertain. It is mentioned in historical records such as the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (871), where the deity "Ruiwakasu no Kami" was elevated to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The shrine later became the Sōja of Oki Province, located near the provincial capital. In 1872, under the modern shrine Ranking system, the shrine was designated a prefectural shrine. It houses valuable historical artifacts, including imperial seals and ritual tools. == Architectural Features == The shrine complex includes: * '''main hall (Honden)''': Constructed in 1793 in the Oki-zukuri style, featuring a thatched roof and separated eaves for the main building and porch. * '''Zuishinmon Gate''': Built in 1852, it serves as the entrance to the sacred grounds. * '''Former Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Designated as an auxiliary Important Cultural Property. * '''Oki Family Residence''': A historic house serving as the priest's residence, reflecting the architectural style of 1801. == Cultural Significance == The shrine is closely tied to local history and culture. It houses: * '''Goryōe festival''': An annual event held on June 5, featuring rituals such as horse racing and portable shrine processions. * '''Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar)''': A sacred tree over 1,000 years old, associated with local myths, including the legend of Yao Bikuni. * '''Oki Province Relics''': Imperial seals and bells used historically in administrative functions. == Designations == The shrine and its associated artifacts hold the following designations: * '''Important Cultural Property''' (1992): Includes the main hall, gate, and Oki family residence. * '''National Natural Monument''': Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar) * '''Prefectural Cultural Property''': Includes the Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Kofuns and the Goryōe festival. == Access and location == The shrine is located near historical provincial government ruins and remains a cultural hub for Okinoshima Town. Visitors can view its traditional architecture and partake in its vibrant festivals. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Islands|en|Oki Islands|WD=Q483146|lt=Oki Islands}} * {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} * [[Japanese mythology]] == External Links == * [https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_tamawakasu.html Oki Tourism - Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine] (Japanese) * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Oki Shrines}} {{Sōja shrines}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{wikidata link|Q11572773}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Added translation template]] [[Category:Architecture of Okinoshima Town]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Edo_period_architecture]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Former_Prefectural_Shrines_in_Shimane_Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Shimane prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese mythology]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Municipal History of Okinoshima]] [[Category:Oki Province]] [[Category:Okinoshima, Shimane]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Oki Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:島根県の Important Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Junior Fifth Rank]] [[Category:Senior Sixth Rank]] [[Category:Shikinai Shōsha]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]]

Haiden |location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|en|Shimane Prefecture|WD=Q132751|lt=Shimane Prefecture}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|en|Oki District, Shimane|WD=Q735735|lt=Oki District, Shimane}}, {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|en|Okinoshima, Shimane|WD=Q1205039|lt=Okinoshima, Shimane}}, Shitanishi 701 |coordinates = {{Coord|36|12|25.5|N|133|18|45.2|E|region:JP-32|name=Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |shrine_Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Minor Shrine), Provincial Shrine of Oki Province, Former Prefectural Shrine |established = Unknown |main_hall = Oki-style, thatched roof |annual_festival = June 5 |rituals = Goryō-e (June 5) }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' (玉若酢命神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|en|Okinoshima, Shimane|WD=Q1205039|lt=Okinoshima, Shimane}}, Shimane Prefecture. It is a designated {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|WD=Q712534|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine. Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushinadahime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to クシナダヒメ}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノヒボコ}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inshū Shichō Gōki|qq=}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|WD=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|en|Mizuwakasu Shrine|WD=Q11549109|lt=Mizuwakasu Shrine}} {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{Commons category|Tamawakasumikoto-jinja}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine |image = File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG |location = Shimane Prefecture, Oki District, Okinoshima Town, Shimonishi 701, Japan |coordinates = {{Coord|36.207083|N|133.312556|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (Minor Shrine), {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} of {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|WD=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province}}, Former Prefectural Shrine|establishment = Unknown |architecture = Oki-zukuri (Thatch Roof Style) |annual_festival = [[June 5]] |rituals = Goryōe (June 5)|location = {{ill|Okinoshima|WD=Q1205039}} |architecture_style = {{ill|Oki-zukuri|WD=Q11659055}} }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|玉若酢命神社}}, ''Tamawakasu Mikoto Jinja'') is a Shinto shrine located in Shimonishi, Okinoshima Town, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} and served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} of {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|WD=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province}}. The shrine holds historical importance and is designated as a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates '''Tamawakasu Mikoto''' as the principal deity. Additional deities include: * '''Ōnamuchi no Mikoto''' (Ōkuninushi) * '''Susanoo no Mikoto''' * '''Inadahime no Mikoto''' * '''Kotoshironushi no Mikoto''' * '''Suserihime no Mikoto''' According to legend, Tamawakasu Mikoto was the child of Ōsubetsu no Mikoto, dispatched to develop the Oki Islands. The shrine's priestly lineage, the Oki family, claims descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. == Historical Background == The shrine's founding date is uncertain. It is mentioned in historical records such as the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (871), where the deity "Ruiwakasu no Kami" was elevated to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The shrine later became the Sōja of Oki Province, located near the provincial capital. In 1872, under the modern shrine Ranking system, the shrine was designated a prefectural shrine. It houses valuable historical artifacts, including imperial seals and ritual tools. == Architectural Features == The shrine complex includes: * '''main hall (Honden)''': Constructed in 1793 in the Oki-zukuri style, featuring a thatched roof and separated eaves for the main building and porch. * '''Zuishinmon Gate''': Built in 1852, it serves as the entrance to the sacred grounds. * '''Former Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Designated as an auxiliary Important Cultural Property. * '''Oki Family Residence''': A historic house serving as the priest's residence, reflecting the architectural style of 1801. == Cultural Significance == The shrine is closely tied to local history and culture. It houses: * '''Goryōe festival''': An annual event held on June 5, featuring rituals such as horse racing and portable shrine processions. * '''Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar)''': A sacred tree over 1,000 years old, associated with local myths, including the legend of Yao Bikuni. * '''Oki Province Relics''': Imperial seals and bells used historically in administrative functions. == Designations == The shrine and its associated artifacts hold the following designations: * '''Important Cultural Property''' (1992): Includes the main hall, gate, and Oki family residence. * '''National Natural Monument''': Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar) * '''Prefectural Cultural Property''': Includes the Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Kofuns and the Goryōe festival. == Access and location == The shrine is located near historical provincial government ruins and remains a cultural hub for Okinoshima Town. Visitors can view its traditional architecture and partake in its vibrant festivals. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Islands|en|Oki Islands|WD=Q483146|lt=Oki Islands}} * {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} * [[Japanese mythology]] == External Links == * [https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_tamawakasu.html Oki Tourism - Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine] (Japanese) * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Oki Shrines}} {{Sōja shrines}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{wikidata link|Q11572773}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Added translation template]] [[Category:Architecture of Okinoshima Town]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Edo_period_architecture]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Former_Prefectural_Shrines_in_Shimane_Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Shimane prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese mythology]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Municipal History of Okinoshima]] [[Category:Oki Province]] [[Category:Okinoshima, Shimane]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Oki Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:島根県の Important Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Junior Fifth Rank]] [[Category:Senior Sixth Rank]] [[Category:Shikinai Shōsha]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]]

Historically, the shrine was also known as "Wakasu Daimyōjin" and "Sōja Myōjin." == Deities == The principal deity is '''Tamawakasu Mikoto'''. Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushinadahime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to クシナダヒメ}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノヒボコ}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inshū Shichō Gōki|qq=}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|WD=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|en|Mizuwakasu Shrine|WD=Q11549109|lt=Mizuwakasu Shrine}} {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{Commons category|Tamawakasumikoto-jinja}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine |image = File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG |location = Shimane Prefecture, Oki District, Okinoshima Town, Shimonishi 701, Japan |coordinates = {{Coord|36.207083|N|133.312556|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (Minor Shrine), {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} of {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|WD=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province}}, Former Prefectural Shrine|establishment = Unknown |architecture = Oki-zukuri (Thatch Roof Style) |annual_festival = [[June 5]] |rituals = Goryōe (June 5)|location = {{ill|Okinoshima|WD=Q1205039}} |architecture_style = {{ill|Oki-zukuri|WD=Q11659055}} }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|玉若酢命神社}}, ''Tamawakasu Mikoto Jinja'') is a Shinto shrine located in Shimonishi, Okinoshima Town, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} and served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} of {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|WD=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province}}. The shrine holds historical importance and is designated as a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates '''Tamawakasu Mikoto''' as the principal deity. Additional deities include: * '''Ōnamuchi no Mikoto''' (Ōkuninushi) * '''Susanoo no Mikoto''' * '''Inadahime no Mikoto''' * '''Kotoshironushi no Mikoto''' * '''Suserihime no Mikoto''' According to legend, Tamawakasu Mikoto was the child of Ōsubetsu no Mikoto, dispatched to develop the Oki Islands. The shrine's priestly lineage, the Oki family, claims descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. == Historical Background == The shrine's founding date is uncertain. It is mentioned in historical records such as the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (871), where the deity "Ruiwakasu no Kami" was elevated to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The shrine later became the Sōja of Oki Province, located near the provincial capital. In 1872, under the modern shrine Ranking system, the shrine was designated a prefectural shrine. It houses valuable historical artifacts, including imperial seals and ritual tools. == Architectural Features == The shrine complex includes: * '''main hall (Honden)''': Constructed in 1793 in the Oki-zukuri style, featuring a thatched roof and separated eaves for the main building and porch. * '''Zuishinmon Gate''': Built in 1852, it serves as the entrance to the sacred grounds. * '''Former Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Designated as an auxiliary Important Cultural Property. * '''Oki Family Residence''': A historic house serving as the priest's residence, reflecting the architectural style of 1801. == Cultural Significance == The shrine is closely tied to local history and culture. It houses: * '''Goryōe festival''': An annual event held on June 5, featuring rituals such as horse racing and portable shrine processions. * '''Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar)''': A sacred tree over 1,000 years old, associated with local myths, including the legend of Yao Bikuni. * '''Oki Province Relics''': Imperial seals and bells used historically in administrative functions. == Designations == The shrine and its associated artifacts hold the following designations: * '''Important Cultural Property''' (1992): Includes the main hall, gate, and Oki family residence. * '''National Natural Monument''': Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar) * '''Prefectural Cultural Property''': Includes the Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Kofuns and the Goryōe festival. == Access and location == The shrine is located near historical provincial government ruins and remains a cultural hub for Okinoshima Town. Visitors can view its traditional architecture and partake in its vibrant festivals. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Islands|en|Oki Islands|WD=Q483146|lt=Oki Islands}} * {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja}} * [[Japanese mythology]] == External Links == * [https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_tamawakasu.html Oki Tourism - Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine] (Japanese) * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Oki Shrines}} {{Sōja shrines}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{wikidata link|Q11572773}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Added translation template]] [[Category:Architecture of Okinoshima Town]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Edo_period_architecture]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Former_Prefectural_Shrines_in_Shimane_Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Shimane prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese mythology]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Municipal History of Okinoshima]] [[Category:Oki Province]] [[Category:Okinoshima, Shimane]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Oki Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:島根県の Important Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Junior Fifth Rank]] [[Category:Senior Sixth Rank]] [[Category:Shikinai Shōsha]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:pages]]

Additionally, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大国主}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|須佐之男命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スサノオ}}, {{ill|Kushinadahime|ja|稲田姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushinadahime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to クシナダヒメ}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主|1=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須世理姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suseri-Hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to スセリビメ}} are enshrined as subsidiary deities. According to shrine tradition, Tamawakasu Mikoto is the son of Ōsubetsu Mikoto, who was dispatched to the Oki Islands by Emperor Keikō. The deity is considered pivotal in the development of the islands, and the ancestral Moriya family, who serve as the shrine's priests, claim descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. However, the name does not appear among Emperor Keikō's children in classical texts, and other sources link the origins of the shrine to the lineage of {{ill|Amenohiboko|ja|天日槍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノヒボコ}}. == History == The founding of the shrine is uncertain. A 1667 text, ''{{ill|Inshū Shichō Gōki|ja|隠州視聴合紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inshū Shichō Gōki|qq=}},'' refers to the shrine's priest as "the kokuzō (provincial head) appointed by Emperor Tenmu." The shrine first appears in written records in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|WD=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}} in 871 CE, where the deity "Zuiwakasu no Kami" was promoted to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|en|Mizuwakasu Shrine|WD=Q11549109|lt=Mizuwakasu Shrine|1=Mizuwakasu Shrine}} {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{Commons category|Tamawakasumikoto-jinja}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine |image = File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG |location = Shimane Prefecture, Oki District, Okinoshima Town, Shimonishi 701, Japan |coordinates = {{Coord|36.207083|N|133.312556|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (Minor Shrine), {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja}} of {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|WD=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province|1=Oki Province}}, Former Prefectural Shrine|establishment = Unknown |architecture = Oki-zukuri (Thatch Roof Style) |annual_festival = [[June 5]] |rituals = Goryōe (June 5)|location = {{ill|Okinoshima|WD=Q1205039|1=Okinoshima, Shimane}} |architecture_style = {{ill|Oki-zukuri|WD=Q11659055|1=Oki-zukuri}} }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|玉若酢命神社}}, ''Tamawakasu Mikoto Jinja'') is a Shinto shrine located in Shimonishi, Okinoshima Town, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} and served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja}} of {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|WD=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province|1=Oki Province}}. The shrine holds historical importance and is designated as a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates '''Tamawakasu Mikoto''' as the principal deity. Additional deities include: * '''Ōnamuchi no Mikoto''' (Ōkuninushi) * '''Susanoo no Mikoto''' * '''Inadahime no Mikoto''' * '''Kotoshironushi no Mikoto''' * '''Suserihime no Mikoto''' According to legend, Tamawakasu Mikoto was the child of Ōsubetsu no Mikoto, dispatched to develop the Oki Islands. The shrine's priestly lineage, the Oki family, claims descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. == Historical Background == The shrine's founding date is uncertain. It is mentioned in historical records such as the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (871), where the deity "Ruiwakasu no Kami" was elevated to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The shrine later became the Sōja of Oki Province, located near the provincial capital. In 1872, under the modern shrine Ranking system, the shrine was designated a prefectural shrine. It houses valuable historical artifacts, including imperial seals and ritual tools. == Architectural Features == The shrine complex includes: * '''main hall (Honden)''': Constructed in 1793 in the Oki-zukuri style, featuring a thatched roof and separated eaves for the main building and porch. * '''Zuishinmon Gate''': Built in 1852, it serves as the entrance to the sacred grounds. * '''Former Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Designated as an auxiliary Important Cultural Property. * '''Oki Family Residence''': A historic house serving as the priest's residence, reflecting the architectural style of 1801. == Cultural Significance == The shrine is closely tied to local history and culture. It houses: * '''Goryōe festival''': An annual event held on June 5, featuring rituals such as horse racing and portable shrine processions. * '''Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar)''': A sacred tree over 1,000 years old, associated with local myths, including the legend of Yao Bikuni. * '''Oki Province Relics''': Imperial seals and bells used historically in administrative functions. == Designations == The shrine and its associated artifacts hold the following designations: * '''Important Cultural Property''' (1992): Includes the main hall, gate, and Oki family residence. * '''National Natural Monument''': Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar) * '''Prefectural Cultural Property''': Includes the Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Kofuns and the Goryōe festival. == Access and location == The shrine is located near historical provincial government ruins and remains a cultural hub for Okinoshima Town. Visitors can view its traditional architecture and partake in its vibrant festivals. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Islands|en|Oki Islands|WD=Q483146|lt=Oki Islands|1=Oki Islands}} * {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja}} * [[Japanese mythology]] == External Links == * [https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_tamawakasu.html Oki Tourism - Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine] (Japanese) * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Oki Shrines}} {{Sōja shrines}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{wikidata link|Q11572773}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Added translation template]] [[Category:Architecture of Okinoshima Town]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Edo_period_architecture]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Former_Prefectural_Shrines_in_Shimane_Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Shimane prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese mythology]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Municipal History of Okinoshima]] [[Category:Oki Province]] [[Category:Okinoshima, Shimane]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Oki Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:島根県の Important Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Junior Fifth Rank]] [[Category:Senior Sixth Rank]] [[Category:Shikinai Shōsha]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:pages]]

The name "Zui" (meaning tassel or adornment) is interpreted as referring to Tamawakasu, establishing the shrine's first historical mention. In 927 CE, the shrine was classified as a minor shrine (shōsha) in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}''. == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Three structures (designated 1992): ** Main hall (1793, Edo period) ** Zuishin-mon gate (1852, Edo period) ** Moriya Family Residence (1801, Edo period) === National Natural Monuments === * The "Yao-sugi" Cedar Tree (1929) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Goryō-e Festival (designated 1965) == Goryō-e Festival == The shrine's annual festival, held on June 5, features rituals including horseback processions and Yabusame (archery on horseback). Participants from nearby villages bring offerings and accompany a portable shrine (''mikoshi'') to a temporary shrine. == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Province|ja|Oki Province|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oki Province|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Mizuwakasu Shrine|en|Mizuwakasu Shrine|WD=Q11549109|lt=Mizuwakasu Shrine|1=Mizuwakasu Shrine}} {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{Commons category|Tamawakasumikoto-jinja}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine |image = File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG |location = Shimane Prefecture, Oki District, Okinoshima Town, Shimonishi 701, Japan |coordinates = {{Coord|36.207083|N|133.312556|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |deity = Tamawakasu Mikoto |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (Minor Shrine), {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja}} of {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|WD=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province|1=Oki Province}}, Former Prefectural Shrine|establishment = Unknown |architecture = Oki-zukuri (Thatch Roof Style) |annual_festival = [[June 5]] |rituals = Goryōe (June 5)|location = {{ill|Okinoshima|WD=Q1205039|1=Okinoshima, Shimane}} |architecture_style = {{ill|Oki-zukuri|WD=Q11659055|1=Oki-zukuri}} }} '''Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|玉若酢命神社}}, ''Tamawakasu Mikoto Jinja'') is a Shinto shrine located in Shimonishi, Okinoshima Town, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is listed as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} and served as the {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja}} of {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|WD=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province|1=Oki Province}}. The shrine holds historical importance and is designated as a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates '''Tamawakasu Mikoto''' as the principal deity. Additional deities include: * '''Ōnamuchi no Mikoto''' (Ōkuninushi) * '''Susanoo no Mikoto''' * '''Inadahime no Mikoto''' * '''Kotoshironushi no Mikoto''' * '''Suserihime no Mikoto''' According to legend, Tamawakasu Mikoto was the child of Ōsubetsu no Mikoto, dispatched to develop the Oki Islands. The shrine's priestly lineage, the Oki family, claims descent from Tamawakasu Mikoto. == Historical Background == The shrine's founding date is uncertain. It is mentioned in historical records such as the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' (871), where the deity "Ruiwakasu no Kami" was elevated to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The shrine later became the Sōja of Oki Province, located near the provincial capital. In 1872, under the modern shrine Ranking system, the shrine was designated a prefectural shrine. It houses valuable historical artifacts, including imperial seals and ritual tools. == Architectural Features == The shrine complex includes: * '''main hall (Honden)''': Constructed in 1793 in the Oki-zukuri style, featuring a thatched roof and separated eaves for the main building and porch. * '''Zuishinmon Gate''': Built in 1852, it serves as the entrance to the sacred grounds. * '''Former Worship Hall (Haiden)''': Designated as an auxiliary Important Cultural Property. * '''Oki Family Residence''': A historic house serving as the priest's residence, reflecting the architectural style of 1801. == Cultural Significance == The shrine is closely tied to local history and culture. It houses: * '''Goryōe festival''': An annual event held on June 5, featuring rituals such as horse racing and portable shrine processions. * '''Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar)''': A sacred tree over 1,000 years old, associated with local myths, including the legend of Yao Bikuni. * '''Oki Province Relics''': Imperial seals and bells used historically in administrative functions. == Designations == The shrine and its associated artifacts hold the following designations: * '''Important Cultural Property''' (1992): Includes the main hall, gate, and Oki family residence. * '''National Natural Monument''': Yaosugi (Sacred Cedar) * '''Prefectural Cultural Property''': Includes the Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine Kofuns and the Goryōe festival. == Access and location == The shrine is located near historical provincial government ruins and remains a cultural hub for Okinoshima Town. Visitors can view its traditional architecture and partake in its vibrant festivals. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Oki Islands|en|Oki Islands|WD=Q483146|lt=Oki Islands|1=Oki Islands}} * {{ill|Sōja|en|Sōja|WD=Q873536|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja}} * [[Japanese mythology]] == External Links == * [https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_tamawakasu.html Oki Tourism - Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine] (Japanese) * {{Commonscat-inline}} {{Shinto Horizontal}} {{Oki Shrines}} {{Sōja shrines}} [[ja:玉若酢命神社]] {{translated page|ja|玉若酢命神社|version=102764407|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{wikidata link|Q11572773}} [[Category:Architecture of Okinoshima Town]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Edo_period_architecture]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Former_Prefectural_Shrines_in_Shimane_Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Shimane prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese mythology]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Municipal History of Okinoshima]] [[Category:Oki Province]] [[Category:Okinoshima, Shimane]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Oki Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:島根県の Important Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Junior Fifth Rank]] [[Category:Senior Sixth Rank]] [[Category:Shikinai Shōsha]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]]
